title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page states a theorem headed 'Th. de Mumford–Nakai', which is the Nakai(–Moishezon) ampleness criterion. Grothendieck recasts it in cohomological rather than intersection-theoretic form.

Setting: X is a projective scheme over a field k and L is an invertible sheaf on X. The following are claimed equivalent.
(a) L is ample.
(b) For every coherent sheaf F on X with dim Supp F >= 1, chi(F ⊗ L^n) -> +infinity as n -> +infinity.
(b') The same, but only for F = O_Z with Z an integral closed subscheme of dimension >= 1.
(b'') For every integral Z there is some n = n_Z > 0 with:
  - chi(L^n|Z) >= 2 if dim Z = 1;
  - chi(L^n|Z) >= 1 if dim Z >= 2.
(c), (c'), (c'') The same three conditions with chi replaced by h^0. So (c'') says:
  - some power L^n|Z has at least two independent sections on each integral curve Z;
  - some power L^n|Z has a nonzero section on each integral Z of dimension >= 2.
(d), (d') Two variants, both struck out with a diagonal hatching: some L^n has a nonzero section, and for every integral curve Z either h^0(L^m|Z) >= 2 for some m, or deg(L|Z) > 0.

Top note: the criterion 'généralise le critère d'amplitude de A. Weil'.

Left margin, a numerical form: for X smooth of dimension d, A·C > 0 for every irreducible curve C, and A^d > 0, with intersections computed in K(X). A further marginal remark seems to say one may restrict to positive n.

The next page gives the proof plan:
- (a) => (b), (c) by Hilbert polynomials;
- (b) => (b') => (b'') and (c) => (c') => (c'') are trivial;
- the converse goes by induction on d = dim X.
The induction uses two lemmas. Lemma 1: if the restrictions of L to all proper integral subschemes are ample, then H^i(X, L^n) = 0 for i >= 2 and n >> 0. So chi > 0 forces sections. Lemma 2: then |L^n| is base-point-free and non-constant. Both are referred to a 'lettre à Mumford'.

The purpose is a sections/Euler-characteristic version of Nakai's criterion, adapted to an induction on dimension. It sits in the cycles/standard-conjectures file, where ampleness and the Lefschetz/Hodge-type positivity matter.
errors: Over a non-algebraically-closed k the curve conditions in (b'') and (c'') fail as stated. Take Z = P^1_{k'} with [k':k] = 2, viewed as a k-scheme, and L|Z trivial: then chi(O_Z) = h^0(O_Z) = 2 for every n, yet L is not ample. One must assume k algebraically closed, compare with dim_k H^0(O_Z) instead of 2, or simply ask deg(L|Z) > 0.

In (b'') the dim Z >= 2 condition asks for chi(L^n|Z) >= 1 for a single n. The proof sketched on the next page (via Lemma 1) only controls H^i for i >= 2 when n >> 0. As stated, a small n with nonzero H^2 could satisfy the inequality spuriously; the safe form is 'for infinitely many n' or 'for n >> 0'. The marginal remark about restricting n may be addressing a related issue. The (c'') version with a single n is fine: a nonzero section gives an effective divisor, and induction then gives L^{dim Z}·Z > 0.

The marginal 'numerical criterion' (A·C > 0 on curves and A^d > 0) is incomplete for d >= 3. Nakai's criterion needs A^{dim Z}·Z > 0 for all integral Z. Curves plus the top self-intersection give only strictly nef and big, which is not ample in general (Mumford-type examples). For d = 2 the statement is correct.

ideas.what: Nakai's ampleness criterion: L ample iff L^{dim Z}·Z > 0 for all integral Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakai (1963), Moishezon (1964); Kleiman (1966) for the numerical theory
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA as far as I know; mentioned in the Grothendieck–Mumford correspondence (unsure)

ideas.what: Euler-characteristic form: L ample iff chi(F ⊗ L^n) -> +infinity for all coherent F with positive-dimensional support (or for all O_Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; follows from Nakai plus asymptotic Riemann–Roch (Snapper)

ideas.what: Sections form: L ample iff L|Z has positive degree on curves and some power of L|Z has a nonzero section on every integral Z of dim >= 2
ideas.modern_name: effective-divisor version of the Nakai criterion (the core of Nakai's inductive proof)

ideas.what: Lemma 1 (next page): if L is ample on all proper integral subschemes, then H^i(X, L^n) = 0 for i >= 2 and n >> 0
ideas.modern_name: standard vanishing step in the inductive proof of Nakai–Moishezon

ideas.what: Questions (next page): can one drop the hypothesis that a section exists in (d)/(d'), and can one drop projectivity?
ideas.modern_name: strictly nef vs ample (Mumford's example); Nakai–Moishezon for proper schemes and algebraic spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (counterexample, c. 1960s, in Hartshorne's Ample Subvarieties, 1970); Kleiman (1966) for proper schemes; Kollár for algebraic spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the Nakai criterion purely through the asymptotics of Euler characteristics: chi(F ⊗ L^n) -> +infinity for all coherent F with dim Supp F >= 1. This is pointwise weaker than the numerical condition, since lower-order terms can drive chi to infinity when L^{dim Z}·Z = 0. It is globally equivalent only through the inductive vanishing lemma. This exact formulation is not standard in textbooks, but it is a modest reformulation.
missed.quote: P. tt faisceau cohérent F sur X tel que dimension supp F ≥ 1, on a χ(F⊗L^{⊗n}) → +∞ si n → +∞
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a K-theoretic/cohomological ampleness test needing no intersection theory. That is relevant to K-theoretic or derived-category characterisations of ampleness. Mostly of historical interest, as it shows Grothendieck engaging with Nakai/Mumford around 1965.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially known circle of equivalent forms of the Nakai–Moishezon criterion. The chi-asymptotic version is a mild, unpublished reformulation. The noted gaps (algebraically closed field needed; single n in b'') are minor. The questions on the next page were answered negatively/positively in the literature (Mumford's example; Kleiman).
transcription_corrections: Top note likely reads 'N.B. le critère indiqué généralise le critère d'amplitude de A. Weil.....'.
In c'') the parenthetical should probably read 'tel que dim Z = 1 (resp. dim Z ≥ 2)', parallel to b''), rather than '(dim Z ≥ 1)'.

Left margin: 'Critère numérique (X lisse de dim d): Ȧ·C > 0 si C courbe irréd ⊂ X, Ȧ^d > 0 (intersection calculée dans K(X)!)'; the transcription's 'cohomologique de c(X)' is probably a misreading of 'calculée dans K(X)'.
Margin 'on peut se borner à n-positifs' is plausibly 'on peut se borner à n positif'.
Both d) paragraphs are entirely cancelled by a diagonal cross-hatching, not just individual words.
